Step: Review the seeded LotStatusCode values
Expected Result: Good, Hold, Scrap, Closed, and Open are all present with the correct Name and Description

Step: Inspect the BlocksProduction flag on each status
Expected Result: Hold / Scrap / Closed block production; Good and Open do not (Open is the die-cast accumulator state)

Step: Close the LOT (Good to Closed)
Expected Result: Transition is permitted and a LotStatusHistory row is written; Good to Closed is the enabled status-change path

Step: Attempt a disallowed direct status change (e.g. Good to Scrap)
Expected Result: System rejects the transition with a clear message
Notes: Lot_UpdateStatus enables only Good to Closed; Hold transitions run through the hold workflow (place/release), Open to Good/Scrap only via die-cast Release/Void. Direct Good to Scrap / Hold to Scrap / Hold to Closed are not wired in the status-change proc.

Precondition: A LOT that has changed status
Step: Open the LOT detail / history
Expected Result: Each transition shows old status, new status, reason, changed-by user, terminal, and timestamp in Eastern time

Step: Place a hold on the container from Hold Management
Expected Result: Container status flips to HOLD and a HoldEvent is recorded
Notes: AIM PlaceOnHold is a Gateway-async step

Step: Attempt to load/ship the held container at the Shipping Dock
Expected Result: System refuses to ship a held container

Step: Release the container hold
Expected Result: Container returns to its pre-hold status (Complete) and is eligible for shipping again
Notes: AIM ReleaseFromHold is a Gateway-async step

Precondition: A Good LOT; Hold Management screen open
Step: Place a hold selecting a hold type and reason
Expected Result: A HoldEvent records LOT, hold type, reason, placed-by user, and timestamp; LOT status transitions to Hold
Notes: Hold types include Quality / Customer_Complaint / Precautionary

Precondition: A LOT already on an open hold
Step: Attempt to place a second hold on the same LOT
Expected Result: System rejects — only one open hold per LOT is allowed

Precondition: Logged in as an operator without elevation
Step: Attempt to place or release a hold
Expected Result: Action requires AD elevation before it proceeds

Step: Attempt to consume or advance the held LOT at a workstation
Expected Result: Operation is rejected with a clear message; the BlocksProduction guard prevents production against a held LOT

Step: Release the hold with release remarks
Expected Result: Hold records released-by user, released-at timestamp, and remarks; LOT status returns to its prior status (Good)

Step: Place a Precautionary hold with no non-conformance record
Expected Result: Hold is accepted with no NCM required (NonConformanceId is nullable)

Precondition: A held LOT where only some parts are suspect
Step: Split the held LOT to isolate the suspect parts
Expected Result: Suspect child LOT can be scrapped while the remainder is released; the split is permanently recorded in genealogy
Notes: MVP mechanism for partial quality disposition

Step: Search by criteria (part number, die, cavity, date range, location) and place a hold on several LOTs at once
Expected Result: Each selected LOT receives its own HoldEvent and transitions to Hold in a single action

Precondition: A LOT that is the source of a completed container
Step: Place a hold on that source LOT
Expected Result: System alerts that associated containers exist and may also need to be held

Precondition: Inspection Entry screen; an item with a published quality spec
Step: Scan/resolve a LOT
Expected Result: The active published QualitySpec loads and its attributes render as an input repeater

Precondition: Attribute form rendered for a LOT
Step: Enter measured values and record the sample
Expected Result: A QualitySample header plus one QualityResult per attribute is written; overall Pass/Fail is auto-computed from limits and audited

Step: Record an inspection against the held LOT
Expected Result: Inspection is allowed against a LOT in any status including Hold

Precondition: A LOT whose measured value is out of limits
Step: Record the inspection
Expected Result: Overall result is Fail and the inspector is alerted; the system does NOT automatically place a hold

Step: Use the one-tap Place Hold affordance
Expected Result: A Quality hold is placed on the LOT from the inspection screen

Step: Attach a file (PDF/PNG/XLSX/CSV) to the sample
Expected Result: Attachment metadata (file name, type, path, uploaded-at, uploaded-by) is stored in QualityAttachment
Notes: Backend built (QualityAttachment_Add/ListBySample procs + NQs + entity script); capture UI limited — no file-upload component wired into InspectionEntry yet

Step: Select a sample trigger (SHIFT_START / DIE_CHANGE / TOOL_CHANGE / etc.) when recording
Expected Result: The chosen trigger is captured on the QualitySample record

Precondition: A LOT inspected with a passing sample
Step: Review the LOT after a passing then a failing sample
Expected Result: A passing sample represents the whole LOT and it continues; a failing sample flags the LOT for quality review (no auto-hold)
